title: Edinburgh Pub Quiz

questions.q: What is the name of the extinct volcano in Holyrood Park that towers over the city?
What is the everyday name of the open-access arts festival that fills the city every August?
Greyfriars Bobby, the loyal dog who kept watch over his master's grave, is traditionally said to be which breed?
Which Edinburgh-born author wrote Treasure Island and Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde?
The run of streets from the castle down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse is known by what nickname?
Edinburgh's main railway station takes its name from a series of novels by which author?
Which fictional detective was created by Edinburgh-born writer Arthur Conan Doyle?
Edinburgh sits on the southern shore of which firth?
A gun is fired from Edinburgh Castle on most days of the year. At what time?
Edinburgh's old nickname "Auld Reekie" refers to what?

notes: Arthur's Seat, an extinct volcano in Holyrood Park; see Historic Environment Scotland or Arthur's Seat (Wikipedia).
Edinburgh Festival Fringe, held every August since 1947; see edfringe.com.
Skye Terrier, per his statue by Greyfriars Kirkyard and Greyfriars Bobby (Wikipedia); accept 'a terrier'.
Stevenson was born in Edinburgh in 1850; see the Robert Louis Stevenson Wikipedia article or the RLS Club.
Castle to Holyroodhouse, about a Scots mile long; see Royal Mile (Wikipedia) or VisitScotland.
Waverley station is named after Scott's Waverley novels; see Edinburgh Waverley (Wikipedia) or Network Rail.
Conan Doyle was born at Picardy Place, Edinburgh, in 1859; see Arthur Conan Doyle (Wikipedia).
Firth of Forth; see Firth of Forth (Wikipedia) or any map of Edinburgh and Leith.
The One O'Clock Gun, fired daily except Sundays, Good Friday and Christmas Day; see Edinburgh Castle (Historic Environment Scotland).
'Auld Reekie' means 'Old Smoky', from coal and wood smoke; see Auld Reekie in the Dictionaries of the Scots Language or Wikipedia. Accept 'smoke', 'smoky chimneys' or 'being smelly/smoky'.
